## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Particles
//
// Bodies for the particle vocabulary of `particles.types.plato`: what each
// declared force field contributes, how a force set is summed, and the step
// that advances a particle.
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Force fields — one acceleration each
//  - Wind — a velocity field, not a force
//  - The force set
//  - The particle step
//  - Stepping a system

library Particles
{
    //==
    // # Force fields — one acceleration each
    //
    // Every force answers the same question: what acceleration does it
    // contribute, given where the particle is and how fast it is going. That
    // uniform shape is what makes the total a plain sum and lets the force set
    // grow without touching the step.
    //
    // Accelerations are in meters per second squared throughout, and none of
    // these reads a particle's mass: the declared types describe FIELDS, which
    // accelerate every particle alike, not forces that a mass would divide.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - World space (Z-up, right-handed).

    // The constant acceleration of a uniform gravity field.
    AccelerationAt(self: ParticleGravity): Vector3D
        => self.Acceleration;

    // Velocity-opposing drag, quoted on the velocity RELATIVE to the medium —
    // pass `velocity - windVelocity`, not the particle's world velocity, or a
    // particle at rest in a gale feels nothing.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_(physics))
    AccelerationAt(self: ParticleDrag, relativeVelocity: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => (relativeVelocity * self.LinearCoefficient
            + relativeVelocity * (self.QuadraticCoefficient * relativeVelocity.Magnitude)).Negative;

    // Tangential acceleration around the vortex line: the direction is the
    // axis crossed into the radial offset, and the magnitude is Strength at one
    // meter from the axis, falling off as one over the distance. Exactly on the
    // axis there is no radial direction, so the contribution is zero.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vortex)
    AccelerationAt(self: ParticleVortex, position: Point3D): Vector3D
    {
        var axis = self.Axis.Vector;
        var offset = position - self.Center;
        var radial = offset - axis * offset.Dot(axis);
        var tangent = axis.Cross(radial).NormalizeOr(Vector3D.Zero);
        return tangent * SafeDivide(self.Strength, radial.Magnitude, 0.0);
    }

    // Acceleration toward (or, for a negative Strength, away from) the
    // attractor: Strength at the center, falling linearly to zero at
    // FalloffRadius and staying zero beyond it.
    AccelerationAt(self: ParticleAttractor, position: Point3D): Vector3D
    {
        var offset = self.Center - position;
        var reach = SafeDivide(offset.Magnitude, self.FalloffRadius.Meters, 1.0);
        return offset.NormalizeOr(Vector3D.Zero) * (self.Strength * (1.0 - reach).Saturate);
    }

    // Curl-noise turbulence: the curl of a smooth vector potential, so the
    // field is divergence free and particles swirl without piling up.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curl_(mathematics))
    AccelerationAt(self: ParticleTurbulence, position: Point3D): Vector3D
        => CurlNoise3D(self.Seed, self.SpatialFrequency).Eval(position) * self.Strength;

    //==
    // # Wind — a velocity field, not a force
    //
    // `WindModel` names a speed and a direction, and nothing else in it says
    // how hard the air pushes. That is not an omission: air pushes through
    // DRAG, whose coefficients are the particle's own. So a wind contributes a
    // velocity, the drag term is evaluated on the velocity relative to it, and
    // no coupling constant has to be invented. A scene with wind and no drag
    // moves nothing, which is correct.

    // The wind's velocity at a point and time. Gusts are a travelling
    // sinusoid: the phase advances with time at GustFrequency and lags with
    // distance downwind, so a gust front crosses the scene at the mean speed
    // instead of the whole scene pulsing at once. Turbulence is the gust
    // amplitude as a proportion of Speed, so 0 is a steady wind.
    VelocityAt(self: WindModel, position: Point3D, time: Number): Vector3D
    {
        var direction = self.Direction.Vector;
        var speed = self.Speed.MetersPerSecond;
        var downwind = direction.Dot(position.PositionVector);
        var phase = self.GustFrequency.Hertz * (time - SafeDivide(downwind, speed, 0.0));
        return direction * (speed * (1.0 + self.Turbulence * phase.Turns.Sin));
    }

    // The combined velocity of every wind in the set.
    WindVelocityAt(self: ParticleForces3D, position: Point3D, time: Number): Vector3D
        => self.Winds.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (total, wind) => total + wind.VelocityAt(position, time));

    //==
    // # The force set
    //
    // The sum over a whole `ParticleForces3D`. Winds are resolved first,
    // because the drag term needs the relative velocity; everything else is
    // added independently.

    // The total acceleration the force set applies to a particle at `position`
    // moving at `velocity` at time `time` (seconds on the simulation clock).
    AccelerationAt(self: ParticleForces3D, position: Point3D, velocity: Vector3D, time: Number): Vector3D
    {
        var relative = velocity - self.WindVelocityAt(position, time);
        return self.Gravities.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (total, g) => total + g.AccelerationAt)
             + self.Drags.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (total, d) => total + d.AccelerationAt(relative))
             + self.Vortices.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (total, v) => total + v.AccelerationAt(position))
             + self.Attractors.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (total, a) => total + a.AccelerationAt(position))
             + self.Turbulences.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (total, t) => total + t.AccelerationAt(position));
    }

    // The same force set read in the XY plane, which is what
    // `particles.types.plato` promises a planar system does: the point and
    // velocity are lifted with Z = 0 and the Z component of the answer is
    // dropped.
    AccelerationAt(self: ParticleForces3D, position: Point2D, velocity: Vector2D, time: Number): Vector2D
    {
        var spatial = self.AccelerationAt(
            Point3D(position.X, position.Y, 0.0),
            Vector3D(velocity.X, velocity.Y, 0.0),
            time);
        return Vector2D(spatial.X, spatial.Y);
    }

    // The force fields of a spatial system, bundled. The system stores the six
    // arrays inline; this is the projection onto the shared force vocabulary,
    // so a cloth and a particle system are driven by the same value.
    Forces(self: ParticleSystem3D): ParticleForces3D
        => (self.Gravities, self.Drags, self.Vortices, self.Attractors, self.Turbulences, self.Winds);

    // The force fields of a planar system, bundled. The declared force types
    // are spatial; a planar system reads them in the XY plane.
    Forces(self: ParticleSystem2D): ParticleForces3D
        => (self.Gravities, self.Drags, self.Vortices, self.Attractors, self.Turbulences, self.Winds);
```
